text:
ashley: saw two eviction waves in us-west2 ~02:10 — about 40% of spot gpus went away. some client requests retried, others timed out. thinking we need a tiny 'gatekeeper' process to coordinate graceful drain + token streaming cutover + request requeue across mixed pools. low-risk rollout (10% canary).
dan: can you sketch the flow? curious how this differs from current drain hooks.
ashley: current drain is per-node and mostly blind to live token streams. idea: gatekeeper runs per-pool, watches node lifecycle events, and does 3 things: 1) emit a short-lived handoff token for active streams, 2) pause new long-running requests on affected nodes, 3) signal runtime to requeue on compatible nodes (including non-preemptible) if available.
simran: love it. that handoff token is basically a bridge key so the downstream can pick up the KV cache and resume, right? we need to avoid duplicate consumption.
jon: duplicate is the tricky bit. we should make handoff tokens single-use and include a small TTL + checksum of session prefix. runtime should try local resume first, then requeue if resume fails.
ashley: exact. rough pseudocode for gatekeeper config we discussed:
```yaml
pool: us-west2-spot-mix
canary: 0.1
handoff_ttl_s: 45
resume_grace_s: 30
requeue_policy: [cross-pool, fallback-nonpreemptible, queue-backoff]
```
dan: what's the expected user-visible latency bump during cutover? we need SLO numbers.
simran: if handoff succeeds, resume should be <200ms (KV stitched locally). if we must requeue and wait for a free non-preemptible slot, could be seconds — we should surface a transient 503 with Retry-After instead of long tail.
ashley: agreed. prefer short error + client retry than 30s tail. also cost tradeoffs: fallback to on-demand increases unit cost but keeps UX intact. gatekeeper should tag requests with "eviction-fallback" for billing.
infra-bot: [alert] preemptible-lifecycle: instance-gnr-42 preempt-notice received at 02:10:08 (us-west2), ETA 120s.
jon: small safety: when issuing handoff tokens, gatekeeper uses monotonic epoch and signs tokens so runtimes can reject stale tokens. also include node_id and seq.
simran: we should add a cheap consistency check: runtime tries local resume and if KV checksum mismatch, it falls back to requeue. avoids subtle state corruption.
dan: roll plan: 1) implement gatekeeper prototype behind a feature flag; 2) integrate with runtime requeue API; 3) canary 10% pool for 48h; 4) monitor resume-rate, tail-latency, cost delta.
ashley: logging bits to collect: handoff_issued, resume_success, resume_checksum_mismatch, requeue_target, fallback_cost_tag. add traces so we can trace token flow end-to-end.
jon: also add a small metric for "handoff_abuse" — how often handoff tokens are requested but not used within TTL. helps detect noise.
ashley: question for ops: any region constraints? us-west2 is our largest spot pool — gatekeeper must be region-aware and prefer cross-az requeue first.
simran: yes, cross-az preferred for latency. cross-region only as last resort — huge egress and compliancy issues.
dan: ok let's prototype. i'll open a PR for the gatekeeper proto and a tiny runtime patch to accept handoff tokens. can we reuse existing token streaming APIs?
ashley: we can extend the streaming API with a small token header: `X-Handoff-Token`. runtime will validate via gatekeeper public key.
infra-bot: [deploy] feature-flag gatekeeper-proto created by dan at 02:31:06
jon: small nit — make sure the gatekeeper's permission model prevents accidental fallback to dedicated for unentitled customers. gatekeeper needs quota checks.
simran: yep. add policy: only fallback for tenants with fallback_allowed=true. default false.
ashley: perfect. i'll write the design doc and link the PR. low-risk canary first. thanks all. :thumbsup:
